title: Prisoners of hope; "your sons, O Zion, against your sons, O Greece"; Judah and Joseph regathered (Zech 9:11–11:3)
speaker: The LORD (through the prophet)
description: Prisoners are freed by the blood of the covenant; the LORD bends Judah and Ephraim as his bow against the sons of Greece and defends them; he will punish the shepherds, strengthen Judah and save Joseph, bringing them back from Egypt and Assyria to Gilead and Lebanon; Lebanon's cedars and Bashan's oaks wail.
in_text_interpretation: Javan (Greece) is named as the enemy.

interpretations.label: Begun in the Maccabean wars against the Seleucid Greeks; completed in the final subjugation of the world-power
proponents: C. F. Keil (1868), noting Jerome's report of Jewish readings
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: the sons of Javan are the Graeco-Macedonian world-power (cf. Dan 8:21); weak beginnings in the Maccabean wars, but 9:14–15 point beyond them. Objection: Mitchell holds "your sons, O Greece" to be a gloss.

interpretations.label: Written under the early Ptolemies (c. 285–247 BC); "O Greece" a gloss
interpretations.summary: Textual reasoning: captives in the East and in Egypt (9:11; 10:10) and a hopeful national spirit fit the Jews' situation under Ptolemy II; the words naming Greece break the rhythm and are a later gloss.

referents.referent: Ptolemaic Egypt and the Seleucid East
